title: telemetry-change-gate-and-metric-stability-scorecard
body:
Purpose:
This working doc defines a lightweight change gate and a compact metric stability scorecard intended to reduce alert churn, prevent accidental metric regressions, and make instrumentation changes auditable. The goal is not bureaucracy — it's to make telemetry changes safe for multi-tenant inference and to create a repeatable reviewer checklist for engineers and PMs.

Context / motivation:
- We regularly see churn from metric renames, accidental tag cardinality growth, and subtle histogram re-bucketing that breaks dashboards and paging flows.
- SRE/oncall time is expensive; a small set of noisy changes cause most of the operator load.
- Current practice is informal PR notes and intermittent rollbacks. Need a deterministic way to evaluate risk before merge.

Principles:
- Keep scorecard simple (5–7 attributes). Score quickly in PR review.
- Changes with score above threshold require canary + stakeholder sign-off.
- Higher-cardinality telemetry must be explicit and documented.
- Owners (metric authors) are responsible for consumer outreach + dashboard updates.

Metric Stability Scorecard (apply per-metric or per-change):
Attributes (0–4 each, integers):
  1) Variance impact (how likely shape/quantiles to shift): 0 none -> 4 major (re-bucket/histogram-extract)
  2) Missingness risk (probability of gaps/partial backfill): 0 low -> 4 high (depends on sampling or client rollout)
  3) Cardinality change (expected unique tag growth): 0 none -> 4 unbounded (user input/uuid)
  4) Consumer criticality (dashboards/alerts/SLOs depending on metric): 0 curiosity -> 4 critical (SLO/alert-exec)
  5) Alert/noise sensitivity (how many alerts may flip on minor delta): 0 robust -> 4 fragile
  6) Query-cost impact (expected increase in storage/query bill): 0 negligible -> 4 significant (order-of-magnitude)
  7) Owner (human maturity/previous changes): 0 mature owner -> 4 no known owner/no followup plan

Scoring guidance (sum of attributes, 0-28):
  - 0–6: low risk — standard PR review; callers/dashboards optional notify
  - 7–12: medium risk — require telemetry-owner review + docs update; run lightweight canary (1h ramp)
  - 13–19: high risk — require SRE/observability sign-off, scheduled canary (24h), dashboard smoke tests, update runbooks
  - 20–28: blocker until mitigation plan agreed (migration path, backfill, deprecation plan)

Change gate workflow (PR-level):
  1) Author adds a short scorecard table to the PR description (copy template lower).
  2) Reviewer confirms score and tags required stakeholders (sre/metric-owner/product).
  3) If score >=13, attach a canary plan and schedule the canary window with oncall.
  4) During canary, run these smoke checks (listed below).
  5) Post-canary: update dashboards and metric deprecation notes (if rename).

PR template snippet (to paste into telemetry PR):
  - Metric(s) changed: inference.kv_cache.hit_rate (example)
  - Change type: rename/label-add/histogram-rebucket/etc.
  - Scorecard: variance=1, missingness=0, cardinality=2, consumer=3, noise=2, cost=1, owner=0 -> total=9
  - Canary plan: create mirrored metric with suffix _v2, route 5% traffic from dedicated test-tenants for 24h, compare quantiles, alert delta > 5%
  - Dashboards to update: ops/topline-latency, tenant-cold-cache-panel
  - Linked tickets: OBS-5123

Canary smoke checks (automated + manual):
  - Automated: back-to-back query of baseline vs v2 quantiles, diff at 50/95/99p; check time-series alignment and missing points
  - Automated: cardinality histogram compare (top-50 tag keys)
  - Manual: quick runbook dry-run — trigger synthetic probe scenario and ensure no new alerts fire
  - Manual: sample traces & inspect span tags for new keys

Dashboard update requirements:
  - Any change that affects metric name or label semantics must include an explicit dashboard mapping: old_panel -> new_panel (widget id optional).
  - Add an annotation for the deployment date and PR number.
  - If an alert threshold is impacted, record before/after thresholds and owner-approved rationale in the PR.

Decommission / rename playbook (short):
  1) Create new metric suffix _v2 with new semantics.
  2) Run dual-writing for at least 7 days for production-critical metrics (longer for SLO-derived metrics).
  3) Notify consumers via shared slack + confluence doc (template) and tag monitoring owners.
  4) After consumer migration, switch read paths and deprecate old metric with retention note.

Automation ideas (MVP suggestions for follow-up):
  - Linting bot that enforces PR template presence for telemetry changes (low effort).
  - Scorecard quick-form in GitHub PR UI (dropdowns that compute sum).
  - Canary harness that can auto-deploy metric mirrors and schedule 5%-traffic experiments.

Example completed scorecard (realistic sample):
  - Metric: inference.token.latency.hist
  - Change: move buckets to log-scale to capture tail
  - Scores: variance=3, missingness=1, cardinality=0, consumer=4, noise=3, cost=1, owner=0 -> total=12 (medium-high)
  - Action: require 24h canary, update SLO calculation tests, runbook edit, postmortem-ready checklist

Checklist for reviewers (quick):
  - Is there an owner + slack handle? (required)
  - Did author include scorecard and canary plan if needed?
  - List consumer dashboards and alerts impacted (must be non-empty for consumer>1)
  - Are there storage/query cost implications? (estimate)
  - Are high-cardinality labels called out and justified?
  - If rename, is there a dual-write and deprecation timeline?

Notes to self / open questions (to iterate in next review):
  - Who maintains the canonical mapping of dashboards -> metrics? (Confluence has a partial index)
  - Should we require dual-writing for any change that touches SLO metrics? (probably yes, discuss with SRE leads)
  - How to measure owner maturity score objectively? (proposal: number of previous changes with <2 incidents in 90d)
  - Do we want the bot to block merges on score>19? (OPS overhead vs speed tradeoff)

Action items / next steps:
  - Share this doc with SRE and product analytics (week of Jan 12). Owner: Maya.
  - Build PR template and small GH Action to enforce template presence. Assignee: Omar.
  - Pilot the scorecard on the next three telemetry PRs touching histograms. Assignee: Jin.
  - Create a Confluence page that will become the canonical metric registry link. Assignee: Ravi.

Contacts / channels:
  - #observability (Slack) for async questions
  - Pager duty: oncall-observability (for scheduled canaries)
  - Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/metric-lifecycle

References / related:
  - OBS-5123 (example ticket for histogram re-bucket)
  - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/441

```

```
